text:
sara_support: Heads up — BrightPay reported a behavior change after the v2.1.0 rollout. Their invoice-to-markdown prompt now returns one long paragraph instead of the bulleted list it previously did. They say the model used to output markdown bullets and line breaks; now bullets are gone.

csm_lee: Customer is getting pressure from their product team; asks for an initial triage.

sara_support: Pasted customer's minimal repro below (redacted IDs). They tested against our hosted API at ~2025-09-01.

```
PROMPT:
Convert the invoice text into a markdown bulleted list of line items with quantity, description, and price.

INPUT:
Invoice:
1 x Widget A - $12.00
2 x Widget B - $7.50
Total: $27.00

EXPECTED (what customer used to get):
- 1 × Widget A — $12.00
- 2 × Widget B — $7.50

ACTUAL (customer sees now):
1 x Widget A - $12.00 2 x Widget B - $7.50 Total: $27.00
```

sara_support: They attached the raw API response body (no front-end rendering) — content shows no newlines between items.

deploy-bot: rollout v2.1.0 -> all regions completed at 2025-09-01T13:12:07Z :white_check_mark:

jordan_se: Can you confirm the exact model id + rollout tag? Any changes to server-side postprocessing or sanitizers lately?

sara_support: Model: "redwood-7b-v2.1.0-quant"; rollout tag: "latest-canary" -> promoted to "stable" on deploy. Customer used temperature=0.0, stop tokens set to ["\n\n"]. No custom postprocessing on their side.

navin_ml: I ran our internal regression harness against the v2.1.0 candidate using our invoice benchmark (10k cases). Metrics: formatting pass rate=98.7% (no noticeable regression). The failing customer prompt is more about preserving markdown/newlines than semantic correctness — our bench probably doesn't stress list-formatting.

emma_cs: Customer provided one raw response header set attached in DM — Content-Type: application/json, content-length matches. No escape sequences.

jordan_se: Could be one of three things: (1) tokenization change collapsed whitespace, (2) generation sampling/stop behavior changed (stop handling), or (3) an accidental strip/normalize step in the API response pipeline after rollout. I'll run a direct identical request from staging against both pre-v2.1.0 and v2.1.0 images.

navin_ml: Also ask BrightPay to run a quick debug call returning the full "choices" object (not the flattened text) so we can inspect token-level output and any hidden control tokens. If they can paste that (redacted) it will help.

sara_support: Customer agreed. Asked them to run this minimal curl and paste results: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2.1.0-quant","input":"Convert the invoice text into a markdown bulleted list of line items with quantity, description, and price:\n\nInvoice:\n1 x Widget A - $12.00\n2 x Widget B - $7.50\nTotal: $27.00","temperature":0.0,"max_new_tokens":128}'
```

sara_support: They returned the full JSON. I pasted the choices array into a thread DM and it shows the generated tokens concatenated with no "\n" tokens between items (weird).

navin_ml: If tokens lack explicit newline tokens, that suggests the model generated spaces instead of newlines. Two quick experiments: run same prompt with explicit "\n-" prefixes in prompt and run with higher max_new_tokens; also compare tokenizer outputs for the exact prompt on pre-release vs v2.1.0.

emma_cs: 
- Added the customer's failing prompt to our private eval set (ticket: EVAL-1761).
- Noted that the customer's prompt includes explicit instruction for markdown bullets — might be brittle.

jordan_se: I'm spinning up a staging job to hit both images now. If we reproduce, I'll roll partial revert on routing for the model and open an incident.

navin_ml: Also check if we changed the "sanitize_formatting" flag in the inference pipeline recently; search diff in the last two PRs. Could be an accidental default flip.

sara_support: Thanks. Assigning priority P1 for follow-up. I'll update BrightPay with ETA and request that they keep the raw choices payload until we say otherwise. :pray:

jordan_se: quick note — if we can't repro end-to-end, next step is to ask for the exact request id the customer saw so we can fetch request logs from the tracing pipeline.

sara_support: Will ask for request ids. For now we have the customer's raw JSON and added their prompt to eval. Will follow up with log IDs when available.

navin_ml: +1 to log ids. If we find this is a model behavior change, we'll draft a targeted test and ship a fix. If it's a pipeline sanitizer issue, rollback plan ready.

sara_support: OK closing for now; will reopen thread with request ids or repro confirmation. Thanks everyone.
